about: ImageDraw calls with a NaN, infinite or absurdly large coordinate, as Pillow draws them
note: args: mode and size (width, height) of the image, background (its one colour before the call) or the array "in", xy as passed (xy_form "pairs": a list of (x, y) tuples; "flat": one list x0, y0, x1, y1, ...), then the keyword arguments of the call exactly as passed (a keyword that is absent was not passed). Floats are float.hex() strings. Arrays are (height, width) for L and F, (height, width, 3) for RGB, (height, width, 4) for RGBA; F is float32. Pillow truncates every coordinate toward zero to a C int before drawing, and an F ink to float32. Here some coordinates are NaN, infinite or beyond a C int: "nan", "inf" and "-inf" are float.hex() of those values. Pillow does not refuse them (its check x1 < x0 is false for a NaN); (int) of such a value is the lowest int on the reference PC, and the arithmetic that follows wraps. The C standard leaves both undefined, so these are the reference build's answers. Only calls that Pillow finishes are here: a thin line with such an end takes it 1.5 to 2.7 s (it walks every pixel on the way), an ellipse outline may never return.
